slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.brief: Light of two stated wavelengths falls on the same metal with given work function; using the photoelectric equation, find the ratio of the maximum kinetic energies of the electrons or the stopping potentials.

stem: Light of wavelengths $310\ \text{nm}$ and $620\ \text{nm}$ falls separately on the same metal, whose work function is $1.0\ \text{eV}$. Given $hc=1240\ \text{eV nm}$, find the ratio of the maximum kinetic energies for $310\ \text{nm}$ and $620\ \text{nm}$ light.

verdicts.working: Photon energies are 1240/310 = 4 eV and 1240/620 = 2 eV. The maximum kinetic energies are 4−1 = 3 eV and 2−1 = 1 eV, so their ratio is 3.

working:
$K_{310}=\dfrac{1240}{310}-1=3\ \text{eV}$; $K_{620}=\dfrac{1240}{620}-1=1\ \text{eV}$; $\dfrac{K_{310}}{K_{620}}=3$

Independent check: Photon energies are 1240/310 = 4 eV and 1240/620 = 2 eV. The maximum kinetic energies are 4−1 = 3 eV and 2−1 = 1 eV, so their ratio is 3.
solution:
Using the photoelectric equation, $K_{\text{max}}=hc/\lambda-\phi$:
$$K_{310}=1240/310-1=3\ \text{eV},\qquad K_{620}=1240/620-1=1\ \text{eV}$$
Hence, $K_{310}/K_{620}=3/1=3$.
